reason: Schedule and feasibility lens. Verdict: refuted as written, but the calendar survives a repair. The cited numbers check out: fn_anatomy_exp39.md has a_never 1907, a_tail 606, linefit 354, swap 2175 (+0.0457), u 706, v 701, detection-side 2929. They come from the exp39 stack, though; x138's readmit and gap filler already recover part of them, so the reachable pool on x138 is smaller. x138 cell 0 l.103/105 and cell 4 l.483-498 write edge_cache/<video>.npz with low_coords/low_score (>= 0.3, unrefined int16). Cell 5 l.1180-1245 builds the pool at score >= 0.5, > 2.0 um from any node, so S_EXT 0.5 reuses it as is. The plan fails as written for six reasons. (1) The earliest GPU slot cannot happen. Friend A is told to WAIT for #34 and has made no commits since 24 Sep 04:12 MSK (CONTEXT l.1543-1545), so sasyami 18:00-23:00 UTC on 25 Sep is not real. vitalii has 0 GPU-h until 26 Sep 00:00. Agents may not push kernels (BRIEF s.3), and a push at 00:05 UTC is 03:05 MSK for the user, so the lab realistically starts at about 05:00-07:00 UTC on 26 Sep. (2) The lab harness is missing from the resource list. build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 allows only divinsert/leafprune (l.12-18). No x138-on-train kernel exists: build_capture_kernel.py is exp51 detection-only. Several pieces are new code, about 4-5 agent-h: the x138 train shards, a post-gap-filler checkpoint, control and 2-4 arm tails per video, and in-kernel official scoring against the train geffs. The idea's 4 agent-h cover only the stage, its tests and the step-0 script, so 'code by 16:00' is really about 22:00-23:00. (3) The protocol counts 36 videos, but SELECTION (18 6bba) + CONFIRMATION (18 44b6 + 18 fresh 6bba) = 54. At about 3.5-4.5 min per video (x138 hidden-run latency; sibling verdict v_divisions_divins-x138-lab-retune_schedule.json), 54 videos plus the CPU arm tails take about 5-6 GPU-h. That means 2 shards of 27, each safely under the REPAIR_DEADLINE_S 27000 s guard. (4) Step 0 cannot run in this container as it stands: there is no Kaggle key and no train data. It needs the exp56 kernel output (its edge_cache must be confirmed in the output) and GT geffs for the 4 dummy clips. The dummy clips are train copies (experiments/_lib/holdout_split.json excluded_public_test_copies), and their GT is in dataset sasyami/biohub-friend-a-b20-cache (tools/package_friend_c_b31_cache.py l.4/57). This works once the user pastes the key, as he offered. (5) Implementation flaw: the guard leaks. Extension (K_EXT 4) placed BEFORE the short-track filter can lift fragments of length 2-5 over MIN_TRACK_LEN 6. The filter then keeps nodes it would have removed, and the 3% added-node guard does not count them, so the node multiplier is not bounded as claimed. (6) The slot is ambiguous: 'after gap filler, before short-track filter' spans safe divisions, the geometry filter and prune-isolated, and extending a fork parent or daughter interacts with the safe-division logic and with #35's insertion. Probability (GUESSES): P(step 0 passes) ~0.6; P(lab gate +0.001 with each embryo >= 0 | step 0) ~0.35-0.45; P(the calendar executes on time | gates pass) ~0.85-0.9. So a gated byteext probe gets scored by 29 Sep 10:00 with P ~0.2-0.25 unconditionally, and ~0.85 conditional on go. The calendar has slack of about 2.5 days.
fix_if_any: (a) Pin the slot: after prune-isolated and before the short-track filter. Extend only tracks that already have >= MIN_TRACK_LEN nodes, or count nodes rescued from the filter inside the 3% guard. Never extend from a node with 2 children or into a fork daughter's first frame. Obey _deadline_degraded (the stage is off after REPAIR_DEADLINE_S). Knobs off must stay byte-identical to exp56 (sha check in build_probe_kernel), and the patch must compose with divinsert (exp57b) in case #35 wins. (b) Step 0 in this container, once the user pastes the Kaggle key (stored for this session only, chmod 600). Download the exp56 kernel output and the GT geffs from sasyami/biohub-friend-a-b20-cache. Confirm that the edge_cache npz files hold low_coords. Also read exp56's log lines 'low-detection pool: N peaks >= 0.5, E on existing nodes, F free' per clip; they answer the junk test for free. Add the 2-4 um duplicate histogram and the FN-GT coverage at 3 um. (c) Build the lab from build_capture_kernel.py's shard pattern (TEST_DIR -> train, per-shard stems) on the exp56 notebook. Checkpoint after gap filler; run the tail per arm (control + primary + (a)-only + at most 2 alternates) into separate geff dirs; score officially in the kernel. Parity gate: the control arm must reproduce the kernel's own final geffs. Use 54 videos in 2 shards of 27 on vitalii after the reset. Do not count on sasyami. (d) Get the user's OK for the main session to push the lab kernel, or accept a start at about 06:00 UTC. (e) Hard stop: if the lab is not scored by 27 Sep 18:00 UTC, drop the line. If the lab gate fails, spend no LB slot. Optional, since slots are plentiful (21) and the lab bias here points to underestimation: a looser 'no harm' gate (each embryo >= -0.0005, node ratio <= +2.5%, added-node GT-hit rate >= 0.5 x annotated fraction). That raises P(scored) to ~0.4-0.5, at the price of a probe the ~0.003 LB noise can hardly read.
realistic_public_gain: +0.000..+0.002 (central ~+0.001; GUESS). x138's readmit and gap filler already take part of the exp39-era a_never/a_tail FN, and integer, head-less added nodes are poorly placed for the swap class. The idea's +0.002 central is optimistic, and anything under ~+0.003 is inside LB noise.
realistic_private_gain: +0.000..+0.003 (GUESS). The mechanism does not rely on edge-network confidence, so the sign should transfer. The size depends on private-embryo density and under-segmentation.
